ruling.recommended_action: Escalate to Ryde Trust & Safety for human review under SAFE-1/SAFE-3: preserve the rider's complaint (sexual/body comments and a question about where she lives, made by the driver after the trip) and the post-cancellation call record; consider interim_suspension of the driver under SAFE-4 pending review. Refer the $5.00 no-show charge to the same reviewer rather than ruling on it, and keep the driver's notification-duty and cancellation conduct on file for the reviewer.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen (SAFE-1/SAFE-2). The complaint states that when the rider called the driver about the $5.00 charge "he kept making comments about my body and asked where I live. I felt very uncomfortable." Nothing in the driver statement or chat contradicts it. Read as a careful person would, this is uninvited sexualised commentary plus a request for the rider's home location directed at a lone rider, causing her to feel unsafe — an intimidation/harassment and inappropriate-conduct indicator under SAFE-1. Because any safety indicator requires immediate human escalation regardless of the filed dispute type (here no_show_charge), and SAFE-3 forbids the AI from ruling on fault or outcome in such a case, I do not decide the fare/no-show issue and do not fix the $5.00 either way. Note the call the rider describes is an off-app follow-up call and is not in call_records (the only logged call is the driver's unanswered 08:46:10 call), so the substance rests on the rider's uncontested account and must be investigated by a human.

Record otherwise (for the reviewer, not a ruling). The driver pressed arrived at 08:44:40 with GPS ~60 m from the pickup point (1.3324, 103.8493 vs pickup 1.33207, 103.8491 — inside 200 m) and stayed stationary there until cancelling at 08:50:20; the 5-minute free wait had run by 08:49:40, he sent two in-app messages (08:45:10, 08:50:10) and placed one in-app call (08:46:10, unanswered). Those elements of NS-1 appear satisfied, but the complaint and the safety escalation take precedence and the post-trip conduct the rider describes is entirely outside the records, so the file should reach a human.
ruling.escalation_reason: Complaint contains sexual/inappropriate comments about the rider's body and a question about where she lives, made by the driver, leaving her feeling unsafe. SAFE-1 requires immediate human escalation regardless of the no_show dispute type, and SAFE-3 bars the AI from ruling on fault or outcome in a safety case. The referred call to the driver is not in call_records, so a human must investigate the driver's post-trip conduct and decide on interim measures (SAFE-4) and on the $5.00 no-show charge.

rejected_claims.reason: Not rejected on the timing facts — telemetry and events support arrival at 08:44:40 and cancellation at 08:50:20 (5 min 40 s), within 200 m and stationary throughout. It is not the basis of the ruling only because the safety escalation supersedes a decision on the no-show charge.

Conduct directed at a lone rider and a request for her home address, i.e. intimidation/location-safety concern under SAFE-1
